usage.scope: Observed assistant message snapshots; provider estimates, not invoice

external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Controlled baseline: largest observed eligible leaf-group CUDA duration, without objective-specific agent selection.
selection.hypothesis: Test whether optimizing this local hotspot improves the complete frozen project objective; local duration is not a predicted project gain.

proposal.rationale: inputs/previous-feedback.txt exists and changes this attempt completely: the previous bundle (trial-b13b4205bb, im2col + strided-batched SGEMM split-K over K=4608, split_k in {1,8,32}) was rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise and objective_not_improved, and it was not a near miss - every measured variant was 2.2-3.0x slower end-to-end than the parent (objective 3.90/4.81/5.26 ms across split_k=1/32/8 vs parent 1.72-1.79 ms). Composing the convolution out of torch operators (im2col, bmm, sum) multiplies per-call dispatch cost on a CPU-bound 1.7 ms workload and, per the observed regression, the GEMM leg itself was catastrophically slow at these skinny shapes. That whole family is abandoned; no torch-op composition remains. This attempt keeps the selected group's three aten.conv2d sites (input 1x512x7x7 NCHW contiguous fp32, weight 512x512x3x3, stride 1, padding 1, dilation 1, groups 1, bias None) but computes each with one specialized CUDA kernel compiled at setup. Observed parent behavior per call (from target-resources.json): cudnn Winograd = generateWinogradTilesKernel (11.4-11.8 us, grid 16x128, block 32x4 - filter tiles regenerated every invocation) + _5x_cudnn_ampere_scudnn_winograd_128x128 (56.0-56.2 us launched as only 16 CTAs of 256 threads for a 512x49-output problem), i.e. 203.0 us of the profiled run's ~514.7 us GPU-busy time in these three calls, and 2 kernels + a cudnn plan-cache lookup per call on the CPU side. The replacement kernel is a direct fp32 convolution decomposed into 16 output-channel tiles of 32 x 8 input-channel chunks of 64 (grid 128 blocks x 512 threads with three independent per-thread accumulators and predicated zero padding), preceded by one cudaMemsetAsync zero-init, with the eight chunk partials combined by fp32 atomicAdd: far more concurrent CTAs than the observed 16, no per-call weight transform of any kind (weights are read in place through their original layout), and a single pybind call instead of the aten::conv2d dispatch chain. Hypothesis (not a measured occupancy fact): raising CTA count from 16 to 128 on the 128-SM bound RTX 4090 and deleting the per-call tile-regeneration kernel cuts these calls' GPU time from ~67.7 us each to the low tens of microseconds; because these are the last three convolutions of the network and the run ends in a cheap tail, a large part of that stage-4 GPU time sits on the critical path of the sync-bounded wall clock, and the removed dispatch/cudnn-lookup work lowers the CPU path as well. Expected effect is bounded (~0.1-0.25 ms on a ~1.75 ms objective); no specific gain is claimed in advance. Safety: build() compiles once via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline (nvcc, cached), then qualifies the kernel on the bound device against F.conv2d on random data - a numerical gate (~1e-3 relative, orders above the fp32 reduction-order difference and orders below indexing-bug errors) and an explicit speed gate (median CUDA-event time must beat the cudnn path on-device) - and any failure of compile, qualification or later per-call guards leaves the pure parent aten.conv2d path with unchanged semantics, so the worst case is 'no gain', never wrong outputs or a slowdown.

setup_work.build_time_gpu_work: One-time nvcc compilation of a single small CUDA source via load_inline during build() (~40-60 s cold; cached in the default torch extensions directory keyed by a source hash, so repeat installs in fresh workers on the same filesystem load the cached .so in ~1 s). Then ~30 qualification launches on the bound device inside build(): correctness check vs F.conv2d and two 12-iteration CUDA-event timing loops (fast path vs cudnn) on random 1x512x7x7 / 512x512x3x3 tensors, all on the current stream, followed by a synchronize. No model parameters are transformed, re-packed or written; weights are consumed per call in their original layout, so no packed-weight pools, no CUDA graphs, and no retained GPU memory are created at setup. Setup allocations are transient (input/output/weight fixtures ~9.5 MB total plus cudnn's own workspace for the reference convs) and are freed by the caching allocator before validation runs; framework lifecycle peak counters may briefly include them, which is not a claim of physical-memory savings.
setup_work.per_call_transients: Per replaced call: one freshly allocated 1x512x7x7 fp32 output (100 KB, same size as the parent operator's output, served by the caching allocator) plus one async memset of that buffer and one kernel launch. No im2col columns, no partial buffers, no workspace, no host synchronization, and no allocation is retained across calls.
setup_work.state_and_aliases: Stateless replacements: model parameters are never written, outputs are freshly allocated tensors (no alias of inputs, weights or previous outputs), and the parent operator's NCHW-contiguous fp32 output layout is preserved exactly. No global flags (TF32, cudnn benchmark, float32_matmul_precision) are touched, so the framework math-policy check is unaffected.

quality_risks: fp32 accumulation order differs from the cudnn Winograd reference (64-channel-chunk partial dots summed via unordered fp32 atomicAdd). CPU fp64 reference simulation of the exact index/tiling arithmetic shows fp32 error of the same magnitude as cudnn's own rounding (~3e-6 absolute on unit-scale activations), far inside the atol=rtol=1e-4 logit tolerance; the previous trial with comparable reduction-order differences measured 3.6-3.9e-6 max logit error and passed.

atomicAdd ordering varies run to run, so repeat outputs are not bit-identical (jitter ~1e-7); both continuous steps are compared to the reference with 1e-4 tolerance, three orders above this jitter, so the check cannot flap.

Exact top-1 requires the winning logit margin to exceed ~1e-5; measured max logit deviations in this family are ~4e-6, so a flip would require a near-degenerate top-2 gap that the reference itself does not exhibit.

Compile-time risk: if nvcc or the CUDA toolchain is unavailable on the worker, or the arch is unsuitable, build() catches the failure and installs pure parent fallbacks - identical numerics, no gain, no quality impact. The same applies if the on-device qualification gates (correctness or speed) reject the kernel.

Signature-guarded fast path with parent-operator fallback covers unobserved shapes, strides, dtypes, devices, bias, stride/padding/dilation and groups; any fast-path exception at call time also falls back to the parent operator, preserving semantics at the cost of the original kernel.

If the bound GPU were not sm_89, load_inline auto-detects the arch when CUDA is visible; a hard fallback env override is only applied when no device is visible. Wrong-arch builds fail at import and are caught by the same build() guard.
